newsitem.title: GERMANY: Flat German shares in two minds at bourse-end.
newsitem.headline: Flat German shares in two minds at bourse-end.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade virtually unchanged on Thursday, seemingly in two minds about which direction to pursue after the release of domestic economic data with conflicting messages for the market.
The DAX index of Germany's top 30 shares closed 1.26 points down at 2,624.44 on trade described by dealers as limited.

Buying was seen as held back by the re-emergence of interest rate fears in the U.S. which drove Wall Street stocks lower on Wednesday, together with doubts over how to interpret new German money supply data and a business confidence study.
"People are sitting on their hands at the moment," one dealer said.
The August M3 measure of money supply grew 8.7 percent compared to forecasts of around eight percent, in principle countering arguments for another German rate cut.
But some economists said the growth was largely the result of an increase in short-term credit and thus not too worrying.
The money supply data was followed by publication of August's business climate index by the respected Ifo Institute which showed a widely-expected but marginal increase in business confidence.
Neither piece of news was however enough of an impetus to shift the market one way or the other.
September DAX futures were livelier in trading ahead of Friday's expiry. The contract was quoted 6.5 points higher at 2,628.5, with December futures 5.5 points higher at 2,645.0.
Chemical group Bayer AG saw strong trade, caught up in rumours circulating London that it might be preparing a takeover bid for British drugs firm Zeneca Group Plc.
Bayer, whose shares gained 39 pfennigs to 55.43 by the close, described the market talk as speculation.
